\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ایماندار} (imāndār)}{ایماندار (imāndār)}]{\ur{ایماندار} (imāndār) — honest}

\label{lesson:UR-C193-imandar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for of course, then the Urdu for regret; a pity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ایماندار}}
\textbf{\ur{ایماندار}} — \emph{imāndār} — \textquotedblleft{}honest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ایماندار}} (\emph{imāndār}) is \textquotedblleft{}faith-holder\textquotedblright{}. It joins Arabic \emph{īmān}, \textquotedblleft{}faith\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian (Lane, root \emph{ʾ-m-n}), and the Persian \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}holder\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imāndār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{imāndār}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for of course, then the Urdu for regret; a pity, then say \emph{imāndār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لالچی} (lālchī)}{لالچی (lālchī)}]{\ur{لالچی} (lālchī) — greedy}

\label{lesson:UR-C193-lalchi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for cowardly, then the Urdu for stingy.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لالچی}}
\textbf{\ur{لالچی}} — \emph{lālchī} — \textquotedblleft{}greedy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لالچی}} (\emph{lālchī}) is \emph{lālach}, \textquotedblleft{}greed\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}, \textquotedblleft{}one who has it\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists Hindi \emph{lālac}, \textquotedblleft{}cupidity\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{lālitya}, \textquotedblleft{}amorousness\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11029).
\end{cousinweb}
